---
title: "Installation"
---

## Requirements

- Python 3.12, pinned in `.python-version` and enforced by `pyproject.toml`
- [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) for dependency management
- About 4 GB of disk space for the environment; the data need far more, see [Data](data.qmd)

## Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/holukas/ms-forests-vpd.git
cd ms-forests-vpd
uv sync
```

`uv sync` reads `uv.lock` and creates `.venv` with the exact package versions used for
the manuscript. It downloads Python 3.12 if the system does not have it. To install uv:

```bash
# Windows PowerShell
powershell -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"

# macOS / Linux
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
```

::: {.callout-important title="Pre-publication state"}
`diive` is resolved from a local checkout (`../../diive`) through a `[tool.uv.sources]`
block, so `uv sync` fails on other machines until release 0.91.1 is on PyPI, the pin is
changed from 0.91.0 to 0.91.1, the block is removed and `uv.lock` is regenerated.
:::

## Running scripts

Scripts import from `src/`, which `uv sync` installs in editable mode. Paths are resolved
from the repository root, so scripts run from anywhere:

```bash
uv run python scripts/30_shap/31_shap.py
```

## Packages

Every runtime dependency is pinned in `pyproject.toml` to the version the published
results were produced with, so `pip install .` and `uv sync` give the same environment.
Transitive versions are in `uv.lock`.

| Package | Version | Used for |
|---------|---------|----------|
| `diive` | 0.91.0 | Parquet I/O, FLUXNET file reading, grid aggregation, heatmaps, ET from LE |
| `pandas` | 3.0.5 | Data handling |
| `numpy` | 2.4.6 | Numerics |
| `scipy` | 1.18.0 | Z-scores, nearest-neighbor search, statistics |
| `matplotlib` | 3.11.1 | Figures |
| `scikit-learn` | 1.9.0 | Cross-validation, metrics, hyperparameter search |
| `xgboost` | 3.0.5 | Gradient-boosted regression; the one pin that changes results |
| `shap` | 0.52.0 | SHAP values via `TreeExplainer` |
| `pyale` | 1.2.0 | ALE curves |
| `statsmodels` | 0.14.6 | Spline row of the threshold robustness table |
| `geopandas` | 1.1.4 | Site map |
| `pyyaml` | 6.0.3 | Settings |
| `openpyxl` | 3.1.5 | Tables for Word |

## Reproducibility

The results were produced with xgboost 3.0.5 and `n_jobs=-1` on a 24-thread machine. At
that version and thread count they reproduce bit for bit across all 208 sites. Both
settings change the fitted trees through the order of floating-point additions in the
`hist` tree method:

- Under xgboost 3.3.0, predictions correlate at 0.995 with the published ones, the mean
  absolute SHAP of VPD is higher at every site tested, and the site-level VPD to soil
  moisture ratio is 6 to 21 percent higher. Out-of-sample R2 is unchanged.
- Under 3.0.5 with a different thread count, the early-stopping iteration at one site
  ranged from 478 (24 threads) to 1021 (one thread), and the site-level ratio from 1.53
  to 1.69.

These differences are per site; aggregates over 208 sites are affected less. The shap
and scikit-learn versions make no difference: 0.52.0 and 1.9.0 reproduce the results of
0.48.0 and 1.6.1 exactly.

## Optional groups

```bash
uv sync --extra era5     # scripts 16a to 16d, ERA5 downloads, need credentials
uv sync --group dev      # JupyterLab, pytest, Quarto, ghp-import
```

## Building the documentation

The site is a [Quarto](https://quarto.org/) website under `docs/`. Nothing is executed at
render time, so no data folder is needed.

```powershell
.\preview_docs.ps1            # live preview
.\preview_docs.ps1 -Render    # build into docs/_site/
```

Outside Windows: `uv run quarto preview docs` and `uv run quarto render docs`. The
published site is built by GitHub Actions on every push to `main`.
